Previously the documented facts-axis miss (websource keyed only on config/.env shapes); CLOSED 2026-10-23 by websource `_parse_labeled_creds` (source 'labeled-leak'), which now mints a labeled_leak credential.candidate for this shape. Ground truth: this block should mint credential.candidate.
Version + script scan of an AD DC (Active). Floor: host up, open ports, nmap version evidence, DC candidate, and the core AD service reachabilities. A service scan never yields creds or foothold.
UDP top-ports sweep. Floor: host up, open UDP port set, and the udp-scan marker. No TCP service reachability is implied by a UDP sweep, and no creds.
Single-port https service scan (443 only). Floor: host up, open port, http reachable. Guard: a single https port must not imply ftp or smb, and a scan is never a credential.

SMB probe with an unauthenticated / guest logon that is rejected. Floor: smb reachable, DC candidate from the host banner, domain learned, and the logon-failure blocker. Guard: a rejected logon is never an authenticated session or a validated credential.

SMB logon refused with STATUS_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION (valid secret, but the account cannot log on this way). Floor: smb reachable and the account-restricted blocker. Guard: a restricted logon did not authenticate the session.

SMB logon accepted (plus sign, no Pwn3d marker). Floor: smb reachable, authenticated session, validated and available credential. Guard: a non-admin logon is not admin access, and it is not a logon failure.

SMB share listing that exposes a Groups.xml (GPP) file worth pulling. Floor: the loot file pointer and a config-review flag. Guard: an undecrypted GPP file is not yet a plaintext or available credential.

HTTP 404 error body (PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest wrapper). STRICTER FLOOR / BACKLOG 2026-10-23: the server answered over HTTP, which proves http.reachable; the curl parser mints that for a clean 200 + Server header (case 25f59588e9ad) but not for this error-wrapped non-200 path, so the reachability fact is a tracked miss (the failures-axis HTTP error-body item). Guard: a 404 is not a credential.

SSH session whose banner discloses the uname string and lands on an interactive target prompt. Floor: OS family and kernel learned from the banner; must not mint a plaintext credential from the banner.

Anonymous FTP login accepted, with a server banner. Floor: ftp reachable, the banner, the anonymous-login fact, and the OS family if the banner discloses it. Guard: anonymous access is not a captured credential and not a shell foothold.

FTP directory listing that exposes backup.mdb (a 5.6MB Access DB worth pulling). STRICTER FLOOR / BACKLOG 2026-10-23: a listing that names a loot-worthy file should mint loot.files the way smbclient listings already do; the ftp listing path does not yet, so this is a tracked facts-axis miss, not a test failure. Guard: a listing is still not a credential or a foothold.
Feroxbuster run with discovered paths. Floor: the web content map. Guard: content discovery never yields a credential.
Gobuster v3 run with real results and a tech hint from the responses. Floor: the content map and the web tech fact. Guard: content discovery is not a credential.
Gobuster v2 banner-only block: the run header printed but no paths are shown in this block. Correct behavior is to mint nothing. True-negative guard: no content map from a banner.
mssqlclient.py interactive session established (SQL prompt). Floor: a database session. Guard: opening a DB shell is not OS admin access and is not a captured credential.

sqlmap confirmed injection with a dump that surfaces databases, tables, and credential columns. Floor: injection confirmed, databases, tables, dumped creds, and a credential candidate. Guard: a DB dump is not a shell on the host.
sqlmap confirmed injection with database enumeration, no dump yet. Floor: injection confirmed and the database list. Guard: a confirmed injection without a dump is not yet a credential.
AS-REP roast that returns a crackable hash. Floor: the asrep hash and a credential candidate. Guard: an uncracked hash is not an available credential and not a windows foothold.

AS-REP request against a user that has pre-authentication required: no hash returned. Correct behavior is to mint nothing. True-negative guard: no asrep hash and no credential candidate from a pre-auth-required response.

GetUserSPNs listing the SPN table (request hashes saved to a file, not shown inline here). Floor: the AD user list learned from the SPN table. Guard: an SPN listing without an inline ticket is not a captured credential.
Reading back a Kerberoast output file that contains a TGS ticket hash. Floor: the tgs hash and a credential candidate. Guard: an uncracked ticket is not an available credential and not a foothold.
LDAP bind rejected with invalid credentials. Correct behavior is to mint nothing. True-negative guard: a failed bind did not validate the credential and did not enumerate users.

Local SAM dump yielding NTLM hashes. Floor: the ntlm hashes, a credential candidate, the SAM loot pointer, and an available credential (the hash can pass-the-hash). Guard: a hash is not a plaintext password.

DCSync / NTDS dump yielding domain hashes including krbtgt. Floor: the ntlm hashes, the krbtgt hash, the NTDS loot pointer, a credential candidate, and an available credential. Guard: domain hashes are not plaintext.
Hashcat cracks a hash to plaintext. Floor: the recovered plaintext and an available credential. Guard: cracking a ticket does not by itself place a windows foothold.

John cracks an SSH private-key passphrase. Floor: a credential candidate (the key), the recovered plaintext passphrase, and an available credential. Guard: cracking a passphrase is not yet a linux foothold.
sudo -l showing a NOPASSWD entry for a specific binary. Floor: the sudo rights, the specific sudo binary, and the privesc lead. Guard: a sudo right is a lead, not yet confirmed root access.
sudo -l showing (ALL : ALL) ALL. Floor: the sudo rights and the privesc lead. Guard: the right to escalate is a lead, not yet root access until a shell confirms it.
rpcclient enumdomusers returning domain accounts. Floor: the AD user list. Guard: enumerating users is not a captured credential.

evil-winrm connection banner only (Establishing connection), no shell prompt shown in this block. Correct behavior is to mint nothing from the banner. True-negative guard: a connection banner is not admin access and not a captured credential.

Successful 200 HTML fetch through proxychains (the S-chain prints OK and the page title renders). STRICTER FLOOR / BACKLOG 2026-10-23: a 200 response proves http.reachable, but the proxychains prefix and the absent status/header lines defeat the curl reachability parser, so it mints nothing. Tracked miss. Guard: fetching a page is not a captured credential.

curl against a hostname that does not resolve (DNS failure, no connection made). Correct behavior is to mint nothing. True-negative anchor paired with the HTTP error-body backlog above: when the error-response parser is built it must NOT fire http.reachable on a name-resolution failure, where nothing was ever reached.

User switch attempt failing with nologin(8) message 'This account is currently not available.' because target account login shell is set to nologin. Wave-B outcomes.js target: classify nologin shell prerequisite rejection as environment-error requiring -s <shell> override.

XML service configuration containing <User Name="..."> block with <Option Name="Pass"> 128-hex digest and <Option Name="Salt"> element. Wave-B Tier-2 shape.js target: command-less XML named-attribute password/hash extraction.

Base64 decode of an application URL route parameter resolving to a relative directory/media file path (<dir>/<file>.avi). Wave-B creds.js false-positive guard: single-line base64 decode output matching relative file paths with media or document extensions must not mint plaintext credentials.

SMB client failing SMB2+ dialect negotiation against a legacy NT1/SMBv1-only server ('protocol negotiation failed: NT_STATUS_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED'). Wave-B target: mint smb.reachable and smb.smbv1 while classifying dialect mismatch as environment-error.
